paragraphs.where: Inner child reparenting, P1
paragraphs.before: I see a lot of connection between reparenting therapy and self hypnosis. They fit well together, though I’d learn to do inner-child therapy sober first, in your ordinary mindstate, since that’s the one you’ll be living in, and get enough Nurturer and Protector in the room before you go deep. When you go into hypnosis the child might come to you. You might see that child in any form. It can be an image, a posture, a voice, a memory, an emotion, etc. It can be any age. It can be any vulnerable part of you. It doesn’t even have to be a “child”, if there is no child there, just work with a protector or whatever you find.
paragraphs.after: I see a lot of connection between reparenting therapy and self hypnosis. When you go into hypnosis the child might come to you. You might see that child in any form. It can be an image, a posture, a voice, a memory, an emotion, etc. It can be any age. It can be any vulnerable part of you. It doesn’t even have to be a child, if there is no child there, just work with a protector or whatever you find.

paragraphs.where: When “your voice” is everybody else’s voice, P1
paragraphs.before: It can be difficult to connect with your inner child if your inner child didn’t have the opportunity to develop. This happens often when you grow up in a situation where you don’t have a private self, for example when your family, religion, or community ‘takes over’ very early in your life. Or you are pushed to achieve very early in life. The result is that you don’t know what you feel, what you want, what you believe, what you like and dislike until you have heard someone else’s opinion about it. If you are in that situation, it can be difficult to follow the advice to ‘love yourself’. You don’t even know who ‘yourself’ is! So you can do reparenting and finding yourself in parallel. For others, it is very easy to work with the inner child, they can feel it easily.
paragraphs.after: It can be difficult to connect with your inner child if your inner child didn’t have the opportunity to develop. paragraphs.where: If you feel an urge to move, P1

You do not need to “act out” the urge, feel that you need to move, shake, release, etc. If you do move and you feel that you are causing yourself pain or other symptoms that you are concerned about, stop moving.

All of them are welcome to the “meeting”. You don’t have to get rid of any of them.

paragraphs.where: Finish without forcing a revelation, P1
paragraphs.before: Ending the session. Don’t feel that you have to end the session with a ‘great revelation’! When you have done as much as you want to do, it is a good idea to find out if there is anything that you need to do to make sure that you can leave things where they are for the time being. This might include thanking parts for their help, or making sure that you do something ‘in real life’ (eat a good meal, put a boundary in place, get some rest, repair a relationship, keep a promise etc). Whatever it is, tell your little one, "That’s enough for today. We’re going back to the life we’re building."

paragraphs.where: Forgiveness without bypass, P1
paragraphs.before: We can not ‘force’ forgiveness on ourselves, it has to come from a place of understanding otherwise it can be bypassing. paragraphs.where: 1. Stretch and release, P1
paragraphs.before: Stretch and Release: Work out what will be supporting you, focus on the feeling of support. You can also focus on where one of your hands or feet is. Either actually, or in your imagination, stretch a little bit, either stretching that part of your body slightly or pressing gently down into the support, and then let go of the effort, just relax. See if there is any difference, even if there isn’t. Do this for no more than 3 places on your body. Think of it as ‘releasing’ as you go through the sequence. Which bit of your body, or voice, needs this? What do you need to support it? Bring your body back to normal movement and return.

paragraphs.where: Learning, entering, and returning, P1
paragraphs.before: Healing the Divided Self, Maggie Phillips and Claire Frederick (1995), pp 24-27, 45-50, 83-90, covers a lot of aspects of this post, such as interactive hypnosis, helping the subject learn how to learn by using other senses, learning self hypnosis, making sure the subject comes back at the end, etc. However, this is a professional clinical book, not a self help book, so be careful about trying to use the procedures used with the cases, etc in this book for solo work (the same applies to historical information it contains).
